findings.claim: Only the formatter templates (Enum, Formatter, StringKeyFormatter, Union) gain `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`. The resolver template is not touched. The acceptance criterion asks that all generated code be decorated, but the generated resolver code is left without the attribute: GetFormatter, the Instance field and the nested helper types such as FormatterCache<T> and the GetFormatter helper class. The README text also narrows the claim to 'All generated formatters'.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageScopeTests.AllGeneratedOnlyTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage. It walks every type declared only in generator output and checks that the type or a containing type carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. Expected to fail on head for the resolver's generated nested helper types.

findings.claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, but System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists on netstandard2.0 and on .NET Framework 4.0+, with AttributeTargets.Class. Generated formatters in projects targeting those frameworks therefore stay counted in coverage, which contradicts 'all generated code is decorated'. The compile-safety criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist. L7 defers to the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageScopeTests.FormattersAreExcludedWhenTargetingNetFramework and FormattersAreExcludedWhenTargetingNetStandard20. They parse the generated code with the NETFRAMEWORK / NETSTANDARD2_0 preprocessor symbols and check the formatter type symbols for ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. Expected to fail on head.

findings.claim: The README states that ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. The attribute ships in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+ (System.dll), so this documentation is factually wrong. It also documents the narrower 'formatters only' scope rather than 'all generated code'.

receipt_plan.detail: Cite README.md:1639-1640 against the API reference for System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute ('Applies to .NET Framework 4.0+, .NET Standard 2.0, 2.1').

interpretations.summary: Formatters only. The `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` attribute is emitted unconditionally (no setting) on the formatter classes produced by EnumTemplate, FormatterTemplate, StringKeyFormatterTemplate and UnionTemplate. It is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. The resolver template is untouched.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: All generated code. Also emit the attribute in ResolverTemplate.tt/.cs on every type the generator fully owns, such as the nested FormatterCache<T> and the GetFormatter helper class. This also covers the default resolver when the generator synthesizes it, and could cover generated members of the user's partial resolver. Drop the `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard, because the attribute exists on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+. Fix the README sentence accordingly.
